title: Connect a calendar from Settings

proofs.run: on the owner's Mac, installed build: Settings, Calendars, press the one button, answer Allow in the macOS window, then open Settings, Replies, Sources; read `rows mac-settings-calendars.list` and the calendars rows of `rows mac-settings-replies.sources` through the control socket
proofs.pass: macOS shows its calendar prompt once; after Allow the pane lists the calendars with their account names; Sources lists the same calendars each with a switch (kind calendar, `enabled` readable)

owner: The owner (or the lead on the owner's Mac): the live macOS prompt and the owner's real calendars cannot be shown on a hidden test copy: the fixture only sets the access state (`fixture calendar-access <not-asked|allowed|refused|will-refuse>`, check lines 120-127). Needs: this Mac's Calendar permission dialog answered by a person, and the owner's calendars. The rig proofs 0-1 settle everything that does not need macOS (one ask, list after allow, steps when refused, Sources feed, switches).
notes: state is outside because the acceptance's live part needs the owner's Mac and macOS Calendar permission; the machine part is proof 0. Code: Sources/Features/SettingsCalendarsMac/CalendarsModel.swift:66-80 ask(), :140-155 pushFeed, CalendarsPaneView.swift:45, EventKitCalendarAccess.swift:7, Apps/mac/App/Info.plist:42 NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription. Cases (checks/settingscalendars-check.py): :194 ask-door-asks-once, :211 allowed-lists-name-and-account, :365 allowed-calendars-appear-on-sources-with-their-switches, :371 refused-takes-the-calendars-off-sources, :379 switching-a-calendar-on-sends-its-events; static cases read the Swift sources (the check's header). The selftest writes _captures/settingscalendars-mac/selftest-mutants.json (line ~827) so run it in a copy that may write there. The aggregate total line is the pass line; no line per case.
